answer: A fake identity pays off only while it costs less than the nectar it farms. Each agent registers an enclave key and stakes a bond scaled by how many agents share its funding source - the tenth wallet from one address pays ten times the first. Each attestation becomes a vertex in a public citation graph, citing two earlier entries, so a fake cluster must reference real work to look alive. A rotating reef of validators replays 5% of entries weekly; identical enclave signatures from two keys, or mutual-only citations, slash the whole bond tree. Fails when replay cost exceeds bond.
